item: first load benchmark against the real search application

hardware.host: Apple M4 Pro, 14 CPU cores, 51,539,607,552 bytes host memory, macOS 26.6.2
hardware.contention_note: k6, Elasticsearch, Redis, and the embedding service shared the Docker Desktop VM; the Java services ran on the same laptop host.

topology: one catalog-service JVM, one search-service JVM, one PostgreSQL 16 container, one Elasticsearch 8.15.2 node, one Redis 7 container, and one pinned BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 embedding container

corpus.provenance: generated seed catalog; not a real assortment
corpus.query_provenance: catalog-derived synthetic queries; not shopper traffic

observed_saturation.cold: The knee is between 25 and 40 requested RPS. At 40, target rate was missed and p95 rose from 139ms to 6049ms.
observed_saturation.warm: Two thousand requested RPS was sustained. At 5000, achieved rate fell to 2988 RPS and transport errors appeared; at 10000, k6 warned that its 1000-VU ceiling was exhausted, so service and co-located load-generator limits cannot be separated.

discarded_runs: Calibration with inherited DEBUG=release was discarded because Spring Boot enabled per-request debug logging.
High-rate runs called warm without preloading were discarded because empty Redis caused a startup cache stampede.
limits: These numbers do not transfer to production: this is one replica per service, a 600-product generated catalog, one laptop, and a synthetic query distribution.

Read path only. Every run here is ops/k6/search-load.js against /search; no order, cart or checkout write was exercised, so nothing in this file describes write capacity, database contention or outbox throughput. ops/k6/shopper-journey.js covers those and has not been run.
Warm results are an optimistic cache-hit bound, not general search capacity.
Thirty-second points are exploratory and include a co-located load generator; they are not a capacity plan or performance regression gate.
The runs predate ops/k6/traffic-model.json. That model governs the journey script only, so it does not affect any number here, but a future journey benchmark must record the model version it used.
